exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = 1 - \dfrac 1 2 \sqrt[3]{x} .$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 1 - \dfrac 1 2 \sqrt[3]{x} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 1 - \dfrac 1 2 \sqrt[3]{y}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 1 - \dfrac 1 2 \sqrt[3]{y} \\[5pt] \dfrac 1 2 \sqrt[3]{y} & = 1 - x \\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y} & = 2 (1 - x)\\[5pt] \big(\sqrt[3]{y}\big)^3 & = \left( 2 (1 - x) \right)^3\\[5pt] y & = 8 (1 - x )^3 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 8 (1 - x )^3 }. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 4\sqrt{x} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 4\sqrt{y}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 4\sqrt{y} \\[5pt] \sqrt{y} & = \dfrac{1}{4}x\\[5pt] (\sqrt{y})^2 & = \left(\dfrac{1}{4}x\right)^2\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{1}{16}x^2 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{16}x^2. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \geq 0, \qquad f(x) \geq 0. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \geq 0, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \geq 0. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Radical Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{x}} - 4 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{y}} - 4. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{y}} - 4\\[5pt] x + 4 & = \dfrac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{y}}\\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{x + 4} & = \dfrac{3\sqrt[3]{y}}{2}\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y} & = \dfrac{2}{3(x + 4)} \\[5pt] (\sqrt[3]{y})^3 & = \left( \dfrac{2}{3(x + 4)} \right)^3 \\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{8}{27(x + 4)^3} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{8}{27(x + 4)^3}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \neq 0, \qquad f(x) \neq -4. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \neq -4, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \neq 0. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac {2} {5\sqrt{x}} + 1.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac {2} {5\sqrt{x}} + 1 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac {2} {5\sqrt{y}} + 1. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac {2} {5\sqrt{y}} + 1\\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{5\sqrt{y}} & = x - 1\\[5pt] \sqrt{y} &= \dfrac{2}{5 (x - 1)} \\[5pt] \left(\sqrt{y}\right)^2 &= \left( \dfrac{2}{5 (x - 1)} \right)^2 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{4}{25 (x - 1)^2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{4} {25 (x - 1)^2}}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x > 0, \qquad f(x) > 1. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x > 1, \qquad f^{-1}(x) > 0. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = 2 - 4\sqrt{x + 3}.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 2 - 4\sqrt{x + 3} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 2 - 4\sqrt{y + 3}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 2 - 4\sqrt{y + 3}\\[5pt] 4\sqrt{ y + 3} & = 2 - x\\[5pt] \sqrt{ y + 3} & = \dfrac 1 4(2 - x)\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt{y + 3} \right)^2 & = \left(\dfrac 1 4 (2 - x) \right)^2\\[5pt] y + 3 & = \dfrac 1 {16} (2 - x )^2 \\[5pt] y & = \dfrac 1 {16} (2 - x )^2 - 3 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac 1 {16} (2 - x )^2 - 3}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \geq -3, \qquad f(x) \leq 2. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \leq 2, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \geq -3. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac {3} {\sqrt[4] {x - 2}} + 1.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac {3} {\sqrt[4] {x - 2}} + 1 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac {3} {\sqrt[4] {y - 2}} + 1. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac {3} {\sqrt[4] {y - 2}} + 1 \\[5pt] \sqrt[4]{y - 2} & = \dfrac{3} {x - 1} \\[5pt] (\sqrt[4]{y - 2})^4 & = \left( \dfrac 3 {x - 1} \right)^4\\[5pt] y - 2 &= \dfrac{81}{(x - 1)^4} \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{81}{(x - 1)^4} + 2 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{81}{(x - 1)^4} + 2}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x\gt 2, \qquad f(x) \gt 1. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \gt 1, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \gt 2. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{x - 3} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{y - 3}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

\begin{align} x & = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{y - 3}\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y - 3} & = 3x\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{y - 3} \right)^3 & = \left( 3x \right)^3\\[5pt] y - 3 & = 27x^3 \\[5pt] y & = 27x^3 + 3 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = 27x^3 + 3. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \sqrt[3]{4x + 1} - 2 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \sqrt[3]{4y + 1} - 2. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

\begin{align} x & = \sqrt[3]{4y + 1} - 2\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{4y + 1} & = x + 2\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{4y + 1} \right)^3 & = \left( x+2 \right)^3\\[5pt] 4y + 1 & = (x+2)^3 \\[5pt] 4y & = (x+2)^3 - 1\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{1}{4}(x+2)^3 - \dfrac{1}{4} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{4}(x+2)^3 - \dfrac{1}{4}. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2x+1}}.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2x+1}} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2y+1}}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2y+1}} \\[5pt] \sqrt{2y+1} & = \dfrac{5}x \\[5pt] (\sqrt{2y+1})^2 & = \left( \dfrac5x \right)^2\\[5pt] 2y+1 &= \dfrac{25}{x^2} \\[5pt] 2y &= \dfrac{25}{x^2}-1 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{25}{2x^2} - \dfrac{1}{2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{25}{2x^2} - \dfrac{1}{2}}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x > -\dfrac12, \qquad f(x) > 0. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x > 0, \qquad f^{-1}(x) > -\dfrac12. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.text:
The function $f(x),$ defined as \[ f(x) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3x + k}}, \qquad x \neq -\dfrac{k}{3} \]

has an inverse function given by

\[f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{8}{3x^3} - \dfrac{5}{3}, \qquad x \neq 0.\]

What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3x + k}} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3y + k}}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3y + k}} \\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{3y + k} & = \dfrac{2}{x}\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{3y + k} \right)^3 & = \left( \dfrac{2}{x} \right)^3 \\[5pt] 3y + k & = \dfrac{2^3}{x^3}\\[5pt] 3y & = \dfrac{8}{x^3} - k\\[5pt] 3y & = \dfrac{8}{x^3} - k \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{8}{3x^3} - \dfrac{k}{3} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{8}{3x^3} - \dfrac{k}{3}, \qquad x \neq 0. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that \[ -\dfrac{k}{3} = -\dfrac{5}{3} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad k = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5}. \]

example.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.text: The function $f(x) = \sqrt[3]{kx + 2} - 2$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{4}(x+2)^3 - \dfrac{1}{2}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \sqrt[3]{kx + 2} - 2 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \sqrt[3]{ky + 2} - 2. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \sqrt[3]{ky + 2} - 2\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{ky + 2} & = x + 2\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{ky + 2} \right)^3 & = \left( x+2 \right)^3\\[5pt] ky + 2 & = (x+2)^3\\[5pt] ky & = (x+2)^3 - 2\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{1}{k}(x+2)^3 - \dfrac{2}{k} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{k}(x+2)^3 - \dfrac{2}{k}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that \[ \dfrac{1}{k} = \dfrac{1}{4} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad k = 4. \]
